subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — initial post-call recap

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call so we have everything aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary workload: checkout fraud-detection + personalization scoring called inline from the web checkout flow.
- Latency sensitivity: global user-facing checkout — want P95 end-to-end inference latency at or below 200ms if possible.
- Throughput: spikes up to ~150 req/sec during peak minutes; sustained baseline ~40 req/sec.
- Data residency: initial rollout in US, potential EU expansion next year.
- Security: SOC2 + audit logs required; no air-gap/air-gapped env needed at immediate launch.

Deployment modes we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding and managed capacity; good for early stages, but can have variability at very high sustained loads depending on plan.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost; recommended when you need strict latency SLOs and steady high throughput.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: for regulated customers needing private control plane — not required for your current rollout.

Immediate questions for you so we can firm a recommendation and put together an estimate: 
1) Is P95 = 200ms a hard requirement for the first launch, or a target we should aim for?
2) Can you confirm the traffic pattern — is 150 req/sec a brief spike (a few minutes per hour) or sustained for longer windows?
3) Any procurement timelines or budget constraints we should be aware of (procurement contact + dates)?

Next steps I propose:
- If P95 200ms is a hard requirement and spikes are sustained, we’ll put together a Dedicated proposal with estimated committed capacity + burst plan.
- If P95 is a target and spikes are short, Hosted API with autoscaling + caching could be viable and faster to start.
- Schedule a benchmark session (we’ll repro your traffic pattern) — can do next week if you’re available.

I attached the mutual action plan spreadsheet from the call (finpay_map.xlsx) so we have the milestones captured.

If you can reply with the three items above (P95 requirement, spike duration, procurement timeline), I’ll pull together the recommendation and pricing options.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below: 

1) P95 = 200ms is effectively a hard requirement for the checkout flow. Anything above that and our conversion degrades noticeably.
2) The 150 req/sec number is what we see during our peak 10-minute windows (roughly 2–3x per hour during promotions). Baseline is ~35–45 req/sec as you noted. So spikes are short but recurring.
3) Procurement: we’re targeting a signed contract by end of May. Procurement lead is Mike Chen (mike.chen@finpay.com). Budget: we have flexibility if the ROI holds — will need a formal quote for dedicated capacity to compare with hosted run-rate.

Can you confirm whether Hosted API with a managed burst/priority tier can meet the P95 200ms SLA for the spike windows, or whether Dedicated is the only safe option? If Dedicated is the recommendation, please send a rough committed capacity estimate + ballpark monthly pricing so I can start procurement conversations.

Best,
Sarah Martinez
Head of Product, FinPay

Neha / Dylan —

Quick recommendation based on Sarah’s answers (P95 hard req, short recurring spikes to 150 rps, baseline ~40 rps):

1) Dedicated is the conservative / recommended path for launch. Reasons:
   - Predictable latency: dedicated pools let us size GPUs and scheduling to hold P95 under the traffic envelope with room for headroom.
   - Cost predictability: committed units -> lower unit costs versus excessive hosted burst usage during frequent spikes.
   - Auditability and isolation for logs/metrics during peak events.

2) Hosted + burst is borderline. It may meet the target in many cases, especially if we combine autoscaling, request prioritization for checkout traffic, and aggressive KV/prefix caching. But because P95 is a hard requirement, the risk of noisy multi-tenant tail latency is material.

3) Recommended next steps (owners):
   - Dylan: run a short benchmark using a representative payload and the FinPay traffic profile (baseline + 10-min spikes to 150 rps). Capture P50/P95/P99 and token cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated footprints. (owner: dylan_brooks)
   - Neha: prepare a Dedicated proposal with committed capacity sizing (we can propose a 2-week PoC in Dedicated mode) and a ballpark monthly price to share with procurement. (owner: neha_kapoor)
   - Schedule a technical benchmark call with Sarah + Mike next week (coordination: neha).

I’ll backfill pricing and escalation paths if procurement requests SLA credits. Aim to keep the PO window to end of May.

-Marissa
